title: Topic 41 · 20 瓦的奇迹 — 神经科学

questions.question: 按文章修正后的皮层能量预算，脑的能量大头花在哪里？
options: 执行高难度认知任务时的额外运算，所以认真思考时全脑能耗会明显地飙升
神经元放电那一刻开闸放电本身，信号越多越密集，花在思考上的能量就越大
合成神经递质和长出新突触，学习新东西时这部分开销占到总能耗一半以上
事后钠钾泵烧 ATP 把离子抽回原位，其中突触后接收约占一半，比放电贵
questions.explanation: 文章说放电是顺浓度差开闸放水，几乎不花钱；真正付账的是事后泵把离子抽回。修正版里接收约占一半、放电约两成，静息漏电又占两成。2001 年的旧表曾以为放电占近一半，后来被改掉了。
questions.question_en: According to the article's revised cortical energy budget, where does most of the brain's energy go?
options_en: To extra computation during demanding cognitive tasks, which is why whole-brain energy use spikes when you concentrate
To the moment of firing itself; the more and denser the signals, the more energy goes into thinking
To synthesizing neurotransmitters and growing new synapses, which takes over half the total when learning something new
Afterward, to Na⁺/K⁺ pumps spending ATP to restore ions—with postsynaptic receiving taking about half, more than spiking itself
questions.explanation_en: The article says firing is like opening a floodgate along the gradient—nearly free; the bill comes afterward as pumps restore the ions. In the revised budget, receiving takes about half, spiking about a fifth, and resting leak another fifth. The 2001 estimate had spiking at nearly half before it was revised.

questions.question: 人脑有 860 亿个神经元，却只耗约 20 瓦。按文章，这两者为什么能并存？
options: 我们平时只用了大约 10% 的大脑，其余九成神经元长期闲置，几乎不消耗能量
脑在进化中缩小了单个神经元的体积，神经元越小，维持静息电位所需能量越少
每个神经元单次放电的能耗都极低，所以即使全部同时活跃，总功率也不会很高
账单跟着同时活跃的数量走，预算只许皮层约 1% 同时活跃，容量与成本分开
questions.explanation: 文章说稀疏是被电费逼出来的纪律：用 20 瓦除以单个脉冲的成本，同一时刻只养得起约 1% 的神经元活跃，就像拥有一座巨大的图书馆、一次只开一盏灯。「只用了 10% 的大脑」被文章明确驳斥：进化不会为常年闲置九成的组织付钱。
questions.question_en: The human brain has 86 billion neurons yet runs on about 20 watts. Per the article, how can both be true?
options_en: We normally use only about 10% of the brain, and the other 90% of neurons sit idle, consuming almost no energy
Evolution shrank individual neurons, and the smaller a neuron, the less energy it needs to hold its resting potential
Each spike costs so little energy that even if every neuron fired at once, total power would stay low
The bill tracks how many neurons are active at once, and the budget lets only about 1% of cortex be active—capacity and cost are decoupled
questions.explanation_en: The article calls sparseness a discipline imposed by the power bill: dividing 20 watts by the cost of a spike means only about 1% of neurons can be active at once—like owning a vast library and lighting one lamp at a time. The “10% of the brain” myth is explicitly refuted: evolution wouldn't pay for tissue that idles 90% of the time.

questions.question: 有人说「做难题很费卡路里，所以用脑之后会饿」。按文章的能量账，哪种说法最准确？
options: 脑的能耗完全由血糖决定，多吃糖就能让脑转得更快，做难题前应先补充糖分
做难题时全脑能耗会翻倍，高强度脑力劳动的消耗接近一场中等强度运动
发呆时脑几乎停止耗能，只有专心思考时才大量调用能量，所以想得越多越饿
任务增量通常不到 5%，大部分开销是不管干什么都在烧的自发活动
questions.explanation: 文章说任务增量通常在 5% 以内，算下来一天不过几十千卡；其余是 Raichle 所说的脑的暗能量。所以发呆在能量账上是全价的；文章也说补糖提高认知的效应零散而且小。
questions.question_en: Someone says, “Hard problems burn lots of calories, which is why thinking makes you hungry.” By the article's energy accounting, which statement is most accurate?
options_en: Brain energy use is set entirely by blood sugar; eating sugar makes the brain run faster, so fuel up before hard problems
Whole-brain energy use doubles on hard problems, so intense mental work burns about as much as moderate exercise
The brain nearly stops using energy when idle and draws heavily only when focused, so more thinking means more hunger
Task-driven energy increases are usually under 5%; most of the brain's spending is intrinsic activity that runs whatever you're doing
questions.explanation_en: The article says task increments are usually within 5%—a few dozen kilocalories a day—while the rest is what Raichle calls the brain's dark energy. Daydreaming is thus paid at full price; the article also says sugar's effects on cognition are scattered and small.
